clue.text: Choose isolated area for a dip

definitions.note: dip is slang for a thief who steals from people's pockets

parts.note: to choose is to pick
a pocket is a small isolated area, as in a pocket of resistance

explanation.surface: Someone selects a secluded spot to go for a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dip' looks like a swim, but it is old slang for a thief who lifts wallets.
explanation.definitionFit: Dip is long-standing slang for a sneak thief working crowds, so it names the same person.

clue.text: Choice made by male after bonus reduced

indicators.note: after says the male letter comes behind the shortened bonus
reduced says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a plus is an extra benefit, a bonus

explanation.surface: A man makes his selection once his extra pay has been cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Plum as an adjective means choice or excellent, as in a plum job; both describe the best pick.

clue.text: Mate ringing leader of workers, good for informal chat

indicators.note: ringing means surrounding, so the mate word encloses the letter

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate, from china plate

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A friend phones the foreman, which is fine for a casual natter.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with mate, shortened to CHINA. W goes inside it, then G.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinwag is a British colloquial word for a relaxed gossip or natter between friends.

clue.text: Exercises involving bodily contact on tugs

parts.note: a physical game is one with plenty of bodily contact
tugs are sharp pulls, or jerks

explanation.surface: Workouts featuring a lot of grappling and pulling at each other.
explanation.walkthrough: PHYSICAL JERKS is a dated British phrase for drill-style keep-fit exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old-fashioned British name for routine keep-fit drills such as star jumps.

clue.text: Screwdriver for one rusty nail, say

definitions.meaning: a screwdriver is a mixed drink of vodka and orange juice
a rusty nail is a mixed drink of Scotch and Drambuie

explanation.surface: A toolbox picture: a screwdriver to deal with a corroded nail.
explanation.definitionFit: Both screwdriver and rusty nail are named mixed drinks served at a bar.

clue.text: Avoid fool heading off

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter, the head of the word, is removed

parts.note: to fool someone is to delude them

explanation.surface: Steer clear of the idiot by cutting him off at the pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' sounds like intercepting someone, but it removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude is to evade or escape, the same as avoiding someone or something.

clue.text: Pip leading performer

definitions.meaning: a pip is the ...-shaped badge of rank on an army officer's shoulder
the headline actor in a show is its lead

explanation.surface: Pip, as in the hero of Great Expectations, is the main actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A British officer's rank pips are small stars, and a show's headliner is its top billed name.

clue.text: Territorial dispute at Newmarket?

parts.note: a gang fight over territory, read literally as a battle on the racecourse grass at Newmarket

explanation.surface: A quarrel over land at the famous racing town.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket is England's best-known horse-racing centre; the turf is both racing itself and a gang's patch.
explanation.definitionFit: A turf war is a fight between rival groups over control of an area or remit.

clue.text: Range of skills identified by agent before engaging acrobatic trio

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, acts as an agent

indicators.note: engaging means holding within, so the word for before surrounds the shuffled letters

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before

indicators.note: acrobatic suggests tumbling, so the letters of the word trio are turned about

explanation.surface: A talent scout spots the abilities of a tumbling trio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' is the poetic ERE here, not a positional signal; 'acrobatic' scrambles the trio before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's repertoire is the full set of pieces or abilities they can call on.

clue.text: Harmony or division by close of play?

parts.note: a unit is a division or section of a larger body

indicators.note: close of means the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Is there accord or a split among the players at the end of the game?
explanation.definitionFit: Unity is agreement and togetherness, which is the sense of harmony between people.

clue.text: Drinking vessel holding litre, say — fill messily

indicators.note: holding means the cup word contains the other letters

parts.note: a cup is a vessel to drink from
to say something is to utter it

explanation.surface: A cup with a litre in it gets topped up sloppily.
explanation.definitionFit: To clutter up a space is to fill it untidily with things.

clue.text: What child may say after bedtime story? I don't believe a word of it!

definitions.text: What child may say after bedtime story?
definitions.meaning: a child wanting more asks for one more tale

definitions.text: I don't believe a word of it!
definitions.meaning: a scornful retort to an obvious lie

explanation.surface: A child's plea for more at bedtime, and a sceptic's reply.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally asks for one more tale and idiomatically mocks a story as untrue.

clue.text: Referee, one trying to put a stop to foul play?

definitions.meaning: a football referee blows a whistle to stop play

definitions.text: one trying to put a stop to foul play?
definitions.meaning: someone who exposes wrongdoing in an organisation

explanation.surface: A match official tries to halt dirty tactics.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the official who blows for fouls; figuratively an insider who exposes misconduct.

clue.text: Rest following musical game with string

indicators.note: following means the rest word goes after the musical

parts.note: Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical
a cradle is a rest, as for a telephone handset

explanation.surface: A break after a musical game played with strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat's cradle is a children's game of making loop patterns with string between the fingers.

clue.text: Cooking technique demonstrated by a posh Greek at home

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A smart Greek shows off a culinary method in his own kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Au gratin describes a dish browned under a topping of breadcrumbs or cheese, a way of preparing food.

clue.text: Early form shown by new boy bagging runs after me retiring

indicators.note: after says the new boy part comes behind the reversed me
retiring means going back, so the word me is read backwards
bagging means holding, so the shuffled letters enclose the runs letter
new says the letters of boy are formed afresh

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A new boy scoring runs once I've gone back to the pavilion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' reads like a batsman leaving the field, in keeping with the cricket runs, but it signals a turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is an organism at its earliest stage of development, before birth or hatching.

clue.text: What's unrestrained over in leading drinking event?

indicators.note: in says the reversed word sits inside the leading word

parts.note: best means top, leading

indicators.note: over says the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: something unrestrained is free

explanation.surface: Is the top drinking event the most unruly?
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's unrestrained' is a phrase standing for a single word meaning loose or at liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: A beer festival is a gathering where many ales are served to drinkers.

clue.text: Silly jokes about Pakistan's first capital city

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go round the extra letter
silly suggests the letters of jokes are jumbled foolishly
first means the opening letter of Pakistan's

explanation.surface: Daft gags about the founding of Pakistan's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' scrambles JOKES to SKOJE, and 'about' puts P around it into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Skopje is the seat of government of North Macedonia.

clue.text: Riding fresh horse towards the coast

parts.note: riding a horse is being on it

indicators.note: fresh means the letters of horse are made anew in a different order

explanation.surface: Mounting a new horse and heading for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An onshore wind blows from the sea towards the land.

clue.text: Merchant banker's last atelier vandalised

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of banker's
vandalised means the letters of atelier are smashed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A merchant banker's final studio is wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merchant banker' looks like one phrase but it splits: Merchant is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer is a trader who sells goods to the public, a kind of merchant.

clue.text: Callas rubbished American opera house

indicators.note: rubbished means trashed, so the letters of Callas are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An American critic slates the soprano Maria Callas.
explanation.definitionFit: La Scala is the famous opera theatre in Milan, where Callas often sang.

clue.text: Film tank tracks

parts.note: a reservoir is a large tank for storing water
to track someone is to dog them, follow closely

explanation.surface: A movie about armoured vehicles leaving tread marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Reservoir Dogs is Quentin Tarantino's 1992 crime movie.

clue.text: Ring precinct for gas

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
a precinct is a zone, a designated area

explanation.surface: Call the police precinct about a gas leak.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a form of oxygen, a gas found in the upper atmosphere.

clue.text: Boss getting rid of one professional cook

indicators.note: getting rid of means a letter is dropped from the boss word

parts.note: a chief is the boss
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A manager sacks one of the kitchen staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a cook who works in a restaurant kitchen for pay.

clue.text: Declines ice-cream cornet and pancake

parts.note: declines means falls, drops
a cornet is an ice-cream cone

explanation.surface: Someone refuses an ice cream and a pancake.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop scone, or Scotch pancake, is a small thick griddle cake made from batter.

clue.text: Former PM belonging to The Athenaeum

indicators.note: belonging to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An ex-prime minister is a member of the London gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: The Athenaeum is a famous London club in Pall Mall.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Heath was the Conservative Prime Minister of the UK from 1970 to 1974.

clue.text: Uniform happening to be short

indicators.note: being short means the word lacks its final letter

parts.note: an event is a happening

explanation.surface: An outfit that happens to be too small.
explanation.definitionFit: Even means level and regular throughout, the same as uniform.

clue.text: Partner improved at all?

parts.note: improved means made better
half means at all in phrases like not half bad, meaning not bad at all

explanation.surface: Has a spouse got any better at all?
explanation.walkthrough: In British English 'not half' can mean 'not at all' (not half bad), so HALF stands for 'at all'.
explanation.definitionFit: Better half is a humorous phrase for one's husband or wife.
